desc: Ideate the core algorithm: Initial inversion count + dynamic updates based on wrapping elements.
Define $L[v]$ (pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j, A_i = v, A_j < v$) and $R[v]$ (pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j, A_i < v, A_j = v$).
Determine update logic: When moving from $k$ to $k+1$, elements with value $v = M - 1 - k$ wrap. Subtract $L[v]$, add $R[v]$.
Implement the solution in Python using a Fenwick Tree (BIT) for initial inversion count and $R[v]$ calculation.
Implement the difference array logic for $L[v]$.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
Check edge cases (e.g., $N=1$, $M=1$, all $A_i$ same, sorted, reverse sorted).
Ensure output format matches exactly (one integer per line).
